To find the rank of $F,$ we first reduce it to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -1 \\ 6 & 2 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 14 & 13 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+7{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns (or alternatively, it has exactly $3$ non-zero rows).

Therefore, $\text{rank}(F)=3.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that a matrix of rank $3$ must have at least $3$ columns and at least $3$ rows. 
So, we disregard the matrix $C$ since it has only $2$ rows. 

Also, the matrix must have $3$ pivot columns. As we can see, the matrices  $A$ and $B$ have exactly $3$ pivot columns.  So, $\text{rank}(A)=\text{rank}(B)=3.$

Therefore, the correct answers are "$A$  and $B$ only."
